pr.title: Dont resolve instance of root in `mir_callgraph_cyclic`
pr.description:
`Instance::try_resolve` on a default trait body method will always fail, since it's still possible to further substitute. This leads to a cycle, since in `tests/mir-opt/inline_default_trait_body.rs`, both `Trait::a` and `Trait::b` need to consider the other to be cyclical, but since we couldn't resolve a body, we'd just consider *nothing* to be cyclical.

The root instance we care about when computing `mir_callgraph_cyclic` is trivial to compute (it's just `InstanceKind::Item`), so just replace it with a call to `Instance::new_raw`.

r? @cjgillot @oli-obk

Fixes rust-lang/rust#143534
pr.author: compiler-errors

issues.title: cycle detected when optimizing MIR
issues.body:
### Code

I tried installing `dioxus-cli`

```
cargo install -f dioxus-cli
```

The crate failed to build with this error

```
error[E0391]: cycle detected when optimizing MIR for `ExprExt::cast_to_bool`                                                                                                  
   --> /home/flippette/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/swc_ecma_utils-7.0.0/src/lib.rs:742:5                                                             
    |
742 |     fn cast_to_bool(&self, ctx: &ExprCtx) -> (Purity, BoolValue) {
    |     ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
    |
note: ...which requires optimizing MIR for `ExprExt::cast_to_number`...
   --> /home/flippette/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/swc_ecma_utils-7.0.0/src/lib.rs:970:5
    |
970 |     fn cast_to_number(&self, ctx: &ExprCtx) -> (Purity, Value<f64>) {
    |     ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
    = note: ...which again requires optimizing MIR for `ExprExt::cast_to_bool`, completing the cycle
    = note: see https://rustc-dev-guide.rust-lang.org/overview.html#queries and https://rustc-dev-guide.rust-lang.org/query.html for more information

For more information about this error, try `rustc --explain E0391`.
error: could not compile `swc_ecma_utils` (lib) due to 1 previous error
```

### Version it worked on

`1.90.0-nightly (bdaba05a9 2025-06-27)` and before (I've only tested back through `1.89.0-nightly (d4e1159b8 2025-06-21)`)

### Version with regression

`1.90.0-nightly (11ad40bb8 2025-06-28)` through to `1.90.0-nightly (5adb489a8 2025-07-05)`

evidence: `Instance::try_resolve` on a default trait body method will always fail, since it's still possible to further substitute.
both `Trait::a` and `Trait::b` need to consider the other to be cyclical, but since we couldn't resolve a body, we'd just consider *nothing* to be cyclical.
The root instance we care about when computing `mir_callgraph_cyclic` is trivial to compute (it's just `InstanceKind::Item`), so just replace it with a call to `Instance::new_raw`.
error[E0391]: cycle detected when optimizing MIR for `ExprExt::cast_to_bool`
analysis.incorrectTransformation: Using `Instance::try_resolve` for the callgraph root caused resolution to fail for a default trait body method, because the method still has an unsubstituted `Self` and can be substituted further. The `else` branch then returned an empty `involved` set. In the mutually recursive default-body example, `Trait::a` calls `Trait::b` and `Trait::b` calls `Trait::a`; each should consider the other cyclical, but the unresolved root made *nothing* cyclical. The historical wrong transformation is therefore: resolve the root with `try_resolve` and, on `None`/`Err`, skip cycle detection and report an empty cycle set.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust MIR functions participating in the Inline pass whose root is a trait default method, especially methods with an implicit/unsubstituted `Self` parameter and mutually recursive default bodies (e.g. `trait Trait { fn a(&self) { ().b(); } fn b(&self) { ().a(); } } impl Trait for () {}`). The issue's real-world case involved `ExprExt::cast_to_bool` and `ExprExt::cast_to_number` in `swc_ecma_utils`.
analysis.originalLogic: In `mir_callgraph_cyclic`, the root instance was obtained with `ty::Instance::try_resolve(tcx, typing_env, root.to_def_id(), ty::GenericArgs::identity_for_item(tcx, root.to_def_id()))`. The code pattern was `let Ok(Some(root_instance)) = ... else { trace!("cannot resolve, skipping"); return involved.into(); };`. Thus if resolution failed, the pass returned an empty `involved` set, meaning nothing was considered cyclic.
pitfalls: Do not assume `Instance::try_resolve` always succeeds for a callgraph root; a default trait body can still be further substituted.
Returning an empty `involved` set on resolution failure hides recursion and can lead to compiler query cycles (E0391), not just missed optimization.
The root instance needed for cycle traversal is trivial (`InstanceKind::Item`); using `Instance::new_raw` with the identity args avoids requiring full resolution.

The added MIR diff test files show `before Inline` and `after Inline` with the recursive call still present (`<() as Trait>::b` / `<() as Trait>::a`); they verify the pass does not crash and does not incorrectly inline the cycle, rather than showing an inlined result.
preconditions: Running the Inline MIR pass (`-Zinline-mir`, test-mir-pass: Inline) on a default trait method
The method is part of a call cycle through other default trait methods
The root instance has generic arguments that are not fully resolved by `try_resolve`
The compiler query for optimizing MIR then encounters a cycle while processing the mutually recursive methods
analysis.summary: Fixes the Inline pass's MIR callgraph cycle detection so that default trait body methods are recognized as recursive instead of silently skipping cycle analysis, preventing an E0391 "cycle detected when optimizing MIR" query cycle.
analysis.testStrategy: Add a `tests/mir-opt` regression test with `// EMIT_MIR_FOR_EACH_PANIC_STRATEGY`, `// skip-filecheck`, `//@ test-mir-pass: Inline`, `//@ edition: 2021`, `//@ compile-flags: -Zinline-mir --crate-type=lib`, and `// EMIT_MIR inline_default_trait_body.Trait-a.Inline.diff` / `Trait-b.Inline.diff`. Define a trait whose default methods mutually call each other and implement it for `()`; check that both panic-abort and panic-unwind MIR dumps are produced without a cycle error and that the recursive calls remain in the post-Inline MIR. Also verify the issue's `swc_ecma_utils`-style pair of default trait methods no longer triggers E0391.
analysis.trigger: A default trait body method is analyzed by `mir_callgraph_cyclic` during MIR inlining and its root instance cannot be resolved by `Instance::try_resolve` because the self type/arguments are not yet fully substituted; cycle detection then returns an empty set instead of the recursive instances.
